_comment: Source of truth for the positions page. Hand-edited when a position is opened or closed; build.py adds the live price and derives R. The thesis is written AT ENTRY - a thesis composed at exit is marking your own homework, and the whole point of the page is that the claim was on the record before the outcome was.
_symbol_note: Yahoo symbols. Japan 225 uses NIY=F, the yen Nikkei future, NOT ^N225: the spot index closes with Tokyo while CMC's cash CFD tracks the future, so ^N225 reads about 0.8% away from the platform and puts the stop distance visibly wrong.
_r_note: 1R is the distance from entry to the initial stop. Every outcome on this page is quoted in multiples of it, so positions of different sizes are comparable.
_balance_note: Update balance_aud when it moves materially. The historical section derives its net P&L from this against the net contributions in history.json, so a stale balance makes the headline figure wrong rather than merely old.

open.name: GBP/CHF
thesis: Sterling yields more than any other currency in the G10 and the franc yields least. CMC passes 2.78% a year of that gap through to a long, so the position earns something while it waits.
The risk is a rush into francs. That happens quickly when something goes wrong in Europe, and a stop 1% away does not survive a gap.

open.name: Japan 225
thesis: A continuation trade on an index that had been trending, with the stop 3.5% below the entry so it sits outside the index's own daily range.
It fell as soon as I was in it and has stayed near the stop since, so the setup I entered on has not done what it was supposed to.
The Nikkei usually rallies when the yen is weakening, and I hold this in Australian dollars, so the currency hands back part of any gain in the index.

open.name: USD/MXN
thesis: Short the dollar against the peso to collect the gap between Banxico and the Fed, which is worth 1.57% a year to me after CMC takes its cut.
Financing is the cheapest of anything I hold. CMC charges 1.28% either side of the true rate here, against 8.24% on natural gas.
The peso does not drift against you, it gaps. A stop is not much protection in that, so what actually limits the loss is how small the position is.
